**Module 3 objectives**

This module introduces widely used techniques for analysing multivariate biological data. By the end of this module, you will be able to:

- Understand the principles underlying **Principal Components Analysis (PCA)** and **Non-metric Multidimensional Scaling (nMDS)**
- Be familiar with the concepts behind **multivariate hypothesis testing** using **permutational techniques** such as **ANOSIM** and **PERMANOVA**
- Be able to **plan and conduct experiments** that test multivariate hypotheses
- Know how to **carry out these analyses using relevant statistical software**
- Be able to **interpret, present, and report** your findings clearly and effectively

:::

## Introduction

For this practical you will:

- Analyse and interpret your own group data using the multivariate techniques covered in the [week 9 practical](302-week09.qmd) (**PCA**) and the [week 10 practical](303-week10.qmd) (**nMDS**, **PERMANOVA** and **SIMPER**, where appropriate).
- Perform additional univariate analyses (**regression**, **ANOVA**) to test further hypotheses using your PCA results.

## What you should have at the end of the practical

By the end of the practical, you should have saved the following outputs for your report:

### Community structure analyses

- An **nMDS** ordination, saved as a suitable image file
- **PERMANOVA** results, in an rtf/doc file
- **SIMPER** results, if justified for your data

### PCA outputs

- A file with your jamovi or R output

### Univariate tests using your PCA results

- A file with your jamovi or R output containing **regression** and/or **ANOVA** results, testing hypotheses using your newly derived PCs

## Your own data

At this stage it’s very easy to fiddle with your data. Is there any reason you might want to standardise or transform your data in any way? Some things to consider:

- Do the abundances matter?
- Are you intending to make every sample equal?
- Would it be worth analysing your data at a higher “taxonomic” level?

If you don’t complete your analyses during the practical, the software will be available to you outside of prac times, and there will be further support in Weeks 12 and 13 for any remaining analyses.
